https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/article.text: Oops, something went wrong U.S. markets closed Equinor and ORLEN Sign Three-Year Norwegian Crude Supply Deal Equinor and ORLEN Sign Three-Year Norwegian Crude Supply Deal · Oilprice.com Charles Kennedy August 20, 2026 2 min read CL=F EQNR PKN.WA NG=F Norwegian energy major Equinor has signed a three-year agreement to supply crude oil to Poland's ORLEN from the Johan Sverdrup field, deepening an energy relationship that already spans natural gas, LNG and renewable power. The agreement will take effect at the beginning of September and covers annual deliveries of between 5 million and more than 9 million tonnes of crude, Equinor said Thursday. The contract also allows ORLEN to receive other crude grades produced on the Norwegian Continental Shelf. More from Yahoo Scout How does this agreement expand Equinor-ORLEN's existing energy partnership? What are the key details of Equinor-ORLEN crude oil agreement? What makes Johan Sverdrup field strategically important for Europe? How does this deal support Europe's energy diversification efforts? Financial terms were not disclosed. At the upper end of the agreed range, Norwegian crude could account for as much as one-quarter of ORLEN's annual oil requirements, according to the Polish company. The crude will be supplied to ORLEN refineries in Poland, Lithuania and the Czech Republic, giving the Central European refiner a longer-term source of oil as the region continues to diversify its energy supply. Johan Sverdrup is currently the largest-producing oil field on the Norwegian Continental Shelf and has become an important source of crude for European refiners. Production at the field is also electrified with power from shore, giving it substantially lower operational carbon emissions than the global average. The deal reinforces Norway's growing strategic role in European energy markets following the sharp reduction in Russian oil and gas flows to the region in recent years. Poland in particular has accelerated efforts to replace Russian energy supplies with imports from Norway and other producers. Equinor and ORLEN already cooperate across several parts of the energy market. Norway supplies Poland with pipeline gas, while Equinor also delivers LNG and is expanding its presence in Polish renewable energy. Equinor is developing the Ba?tyk offshore wind projects in the Baltic Sea with Polish utility Polenergia. Its Wento subsidiary is also building a portfolio of onshore wind, solar and battery storage projects in Poland. For ORLEN, the crude agreement provides greater supply visibility amid continued volatility in global oil markets, while giving Equinor a major long-term customer for barrels produced from Norway's largest oil field. On Thursday, Der Spiegel published internal comments on an interview by Elif Eralp, who led the socialist Left Party (Die Linke) to victory in September's state election. Her office had accidentally included the remarks while approving an interview for publication. In the notes, Eralp expressed fears for her family's safety if she publicly named Ibrahim Ibrahim, a pro-Palestinian activist who is reported to have links to the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), which the EU designates a terrorist organization. Ibrahim had attended the Left Party's election-night celebrations and was photographed with prominent Left Party Bundestag member Ferat Koçak. Eralp also cited advice she received from Berlin police against publicly naming individuals linked to organized crime, though that advice was reportedly related to a separate case. Der Spiegel questioned whether her fears could affect her independence as mayor. Eralp rejected suggestions that she could be intimidated and pledged firm action against terrorism and organized crime. She is reportedly considering legal action against the magazine and a complaint to Germany's Press Council. The magazine has also faced criticism for publishing remarks intended for internal use, raising questions about the balance between public interest, privacy, and journalistic ethics. The timing is significant. Eralp, the daughter of Turkish immigrants, could become Berlin's first Left Party mayor and the first woman of Turkish descent to hold the office. Her party won 25.7% of the vote in September's election and hopes to form a government with the center-left Social Democrats (SPD) and the Greens. Both prospective partners have approved formal coalition negotiations. The Left must decide whether to follow suit at a party conference this Saturday, October 31. The far-left party is also facing accusations of antisemitism involving some of its members. Newly elected lawmaker Vanessa Emde faces possible exclusion from the Left's parliamentary group following comments questioning whether states, including Israel, have an inherent right to exist. The Left has been part of Berlin coalition governments before but has never led one. The controversy comes at a pivotal moment in its effort to do so. After his arrival at Panama City airport, Wadephul handed over humanitarian supplies to his Panamanian counterpart Javier Martinez-Acha Vasquez. The aid shipment is made up of about 20 tons of supplies. Panama was hit by a powerful earthquake earlier this month . The supplies include water filters, blankets, tarpaulins, cots and kitchen sets worth over €150,000 ($167,000). More than 5,000 people are still being housed in emergency shelters, weeks after the magnitude-7.7 quake on October 9, which resulted in injuries and damaged hundreds of buildings. Wadephul also thanked the Central American country for maintaining the Panama Canal "so responsibly and ensuring it is fit for the future, as well as more generally focusing on preserving balance in the region." Restrictions on other sea routes due to the conflict in the Middle East has meant that the Panama Canal is more important to global trade than ever. Wadephul is due to hold talks on Thursday with Martinez-Acha Vasquez and President Jose Raul Mulino. Wadephul will travel to the US state of Georgia for the G20 summit in Atlanta on Friday and Saturday. In the university sports hall, the two faced each other, accompanied by two Chinese participants — a referee and the university president. Right from the start, Steinmeier downplayed his chances, and subsequently lost 1–7. Boll, who won silver at the Beijing Olympics in 2008, is the most successful German table tennis player of all time. He won several Olympic medals, as well as titles in World Cups and World Championships during his storied career, which saw him ranked as the number 1 player in the world in 2003, 2011 and 2018. To this day, Boll remains one of the best-known Germans in China, where ping-pong is unofficially considered the national sport. Boll is accompanying Steinmeier as a special guest on his state visit. Boll (left) is a popular figure in China Image: Katharina Kausche/dpa/picture alliance Edited by: Roshni Majumdar https://p.dw.com/p/5Op37 Skip next section Steinmeier calls for fair trade in China during Bejiing visit 10/29/2026 October 29, 2026 Steinmeier calls for fair trade in China during Bejiing visit Rosalia Romaniec in Beijing Steinmeier received an honorary professorship from Peking University president He Guangcai Image: Katharina Kausche/dpa/picture alliance Germany's President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Thursday called on China to reduce economic imbalances between the two countries, as well as between China and Europe. Steinmeier, who was speaking at the renowned Peking University, also urged China to work with Germany and other European nations to strengthen the international, rules-based order and "to advocate for peace and free global trade." The German president, who holds a largely ceremonial role, spoke of his respect for China's rapid development in its economy, technology and politics, calling China a "defining world power." But Steinmeier added, "With greatness and power comes great responsibility." "We are not concerned about China's rise. We are watching how China rises," he said. "We do not want to decouple from China; on the contrary, we want to structure trade in such a way that it continues to benefit both sides." This, he said, requires fair and uniform rules. Steinmeier was referring to the high barriers European companies face when trying to operate in the Chinese market. Since China heavily subsidizes its exports to Europe, the European market comes under pressure too quickly. This poses "the danger of one-sided vulnerability," Steinmeier said. Europeans cannot want this for their economy, just as "China does not want it for its economy." What did Steinmeier say about China and the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East? He also called on China to exert more influence on Russia to bring the war in Ukraine to an end. According to Steinmeier, China's interests are also at stake in this war, just as they are in the Middle East. As a major trading power, China also needs free sea lanes, intact supply chains, and a secure energy supply. "The longer these conflicts persist, the weaker the global economy as a whole becomes — and with it, one of its largest economies: China," the president said. Steinmeier addressed future issues in which China should take a particular interest: climate change and artificial intelligence. He appealed to his hosts, saying that when it comes to AI, "we should jointly establish international guidelines so that the technology remains under human control," he said. On the final day of his state visit, Steinmeier will meet with China's leadership and hold talks with, among others, President Xi Jinping. Steinmeier is making his first visit to China in eight years, as he seeks to boost bilateral ties. After a meeting in Seoul with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Merz highlighted that Russia was supplying weapons to North Korea. The chancellor said this arrangement therefore shows how "Korea's security affects Europe's security. And Europe's security also affects Korea's security." North Korea has boosted its military ties with Russia since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Pyongyang has provided Moscow with artillery ammunition and missiles. It has also, according to South Korean intelligence services, sent about 15,000 soldiers to fight alongside Russian forces. In exchange, Russia provides financial backing, military technology and security guarantees to North Korea. Before Merz's arrival on Thursday, North Korea fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward the Sea of Japan, according to the South Korean military. At the start of his visit, Merz said he hoped that Korea would eventually be unified. The peninsula has been split along the 38th parallel since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953. Merz also agreed with Lee to deepen their two nations' strategic and security ties, which includes joint military exercises and exchange of intelligence. The chancellor is expected to conclude his trip to South Korea with a visit to the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on Friday.
